title: Using NEWS2 / MEOWS observations
summary: Why modified obstetric early warning scores exist, and how to respond to a trigger.

blocks.heading: What it is
bullets: A modified early warning score (MEOWS) adapts general adult early-warning scoring (NEWS2) to pregnancy-specific physiology — for example, the higher resting heart rate and lower blood pressure seen in normal pregnancy — so that deterioration is picked up appropriately rather than masked or over-triggered.
VERIFY the exact scoring chart and trigger thresholds used locally, as these vary between trusts.

blocks.heading: Why it matters
bullets: MBRRACE-UK maternal mortality reviews repeatedly highlight delayed recognition of deterioration — especially in sepsis and haemorrhage — as a preventable factor in maternal deaths.

blocks.heading: Responding to a trigger
bullets: Do not wait to see if it resolves — follow the local escalation protocol for the trigger score reached.
A single very abnormal parameter can warrant escalation even if the total score is not high — VERIFY local 'red' single-parameter triggers.

blocks.heading: Trust your instinct
bullets: A feeling that 'something isn't right' — from the woman, her birth partner, or you — is itself a legitimate reason to escalate, independent of the numerical score.

citations.section: Maternal mortality reports — delayed recognition of deterioration as a recurring preventable factor
